circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, the 5. 281-kilometer Yas Marina Circuit was designed by Hermann Tilke and has served as the venue for Formula One's season-concluding Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One circuit to be constructed, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit, located around the lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosts the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside various supporting racing series. The venue maintains an FIA Grade 1 licence status as a street-based motorsport facility.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Styria, the 4. 326 km circuit has hosted the Austrian Grand Prix across two distinct periods in its history. Originally constructed as the Österreichring, it held the grand prix annually from 1970 to 1987 before undergoing significant modifications, shortening, and rebranding as the A1-Ring to accommodate another seven-year tenure from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street racing venue in Azerbaijan's capital city, positioned alongside Baku Boulevard, with a lap distance of 6. 003 km that ranks as the fourth-longest on the Formula One calendar. Formula One racing began there in 2016 with the European Grand Prix, followed by the inaugural Azerbaijan Grand Prix in 2017, both operated by the Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: The Bahrain International Circuit, a 5. 412 km facility that opened in 2004, hosts the annual Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, marking the championship's first Middle Eastern venue. Beyond Formula One, the track accommodates various motorsport categories including GP2 racing, 24-hour endurance competitions, and previously featured Australian V8 Supercars until 2010, while maintaining FIA Grade 1 certification with multiple alternative configurations available.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit features a balanced mix of high-speed straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a comprehensive test of driving skill. The venue accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators and holds the highest FIA safety certification.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Spa is a 7. 004 km Belgian racing circuit situated near the town of Spa in Wallonia, which has been the home of the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix since 1950. The track has maintained an uninterrupted presence on the F1 calendar since 1985, missing only the 2003 and 2006 seasons.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometre street circuit that serves as the permanent home of the FIA Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the venue has attracted various international motorsport series, including the World Sportscar Championship, Champ Car World Series, and multiple NASCAR competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this motorsport facility hosted the Chinese Grand Prix from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024, establishing itself as the signature venue for China's premier racing event. The track has expanded its motorsport calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near villages in Northamptonshire, Silverstone has been the primary home of Britain's Formula One Grand Prix since 1948, establishing itself as a permanent venue from 1987 after sharing the event with two other circuits during the preceding decades. The track holds particular significance as the venue for the 1950 British Grand Prix, which marked the inaugural race of the World Championship. Beyond Formula One, the circuit also stages MotoGP racing events.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, situated near Budapest in Mogyoród, Hungary, is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held within the Eastern Bloc in 1986. Built in just eight months starting from October 1985, making it the fastest-constructed Formula One venue at that time, the purpose-built facility was chosen over a proposed street circuit in Budapest's central park due to government preference for a dedicated racing venue adjacent to a major highway.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza near Milan is a 5. 793 km Italian racing venue constructed in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built circuit. Since 1949, it has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix, earning the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its notably lengthy straights and fast-paced corner design.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese racetrack operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, with a seating capacity of 155,000 spectators. The venue serves as a prominent host for Formula One races and the Japanese Super Formula championship series.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street track laid out through Paradise, Nevada, featuring a route that navigates the famous boulevard lined with major hotels and casinos. The course incorporates several iconic Las Vegas landmarks, including the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, creating a unique urban racing environment in the heart of the entertainment district.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring two racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who both died in racing accidents in 1962 and 1971 respectively. The track has hosted the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix intermittently, with its current hosting period beginning in 2015 after a 23-year absence, now branded as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary street circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida, spanning 3. 363 miles with 19 corners and an average qualifying speed of approximately 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design, the track was purpose-built to host the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One calendar starting in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco stretches 3. 337 kilometers through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, winding around Monaco's harbor. Though officially designated by its full name, the track is widely known simply as "Monte Carlo" since most of the circuit runs within that particular neighborhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259-kilometre track that restored the Dutch Grand Prix to Formula One's calendar in 2021 after a lengthy absence. The venue will host the championship for the final time in 2026, concluding its partnership with the sport.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit sits near the city of Lusail, north of Doha in Qatar, and spans 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km circuit in São Paulo, Brazil, originally opened in 1940 and renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal aircraft accident in 1977. The counterclockwise track hosts major motorsport events and features an associated kart facility dedicated to compatriot Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track positioned along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that serves as the venue for the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix in Formula One, which began there in 2021. The circuit also accommodates Formula E racing starting in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Downtown Core and Kallang districts, forming a road course that traces the perimeter of Marina Bay.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this Spanish racing facility spans 4. 657 kilometres and features a diverse mix of extended straightaways and varied corner configurations, making it a comprehensive test of driver and vehicle capabilities. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas spans 3. 426 miles and meets the highest FIA standards for motorsport facilities. It currently hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside MotoGP and endurance racing events, while previously staging various other international motorsport competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a racing driver of Thai and British nationality who currently drives for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championships in 2005 and 2006 with Renault and 32 grand prix victories over 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved significant success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24 Hours victories with Toyota and the 2018-19 FIA World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli, an Italian driver, made his Formula One debut in 2025 with Mercedes, where he currently races. He has already secured six Grand Prix victories early in his career.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One, representing Audi in the championship. The talented racer has established himself as a competitive force on the grid with the German manufacturer.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas competes for Cadillac in Formula One and has established himself as a consistent performer across a 13-season career. He achieved runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during consecutive years with Mercedes, while accumulating 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his time in the sport.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto represents Argentina in Formula One, currently racing for the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan combines endurance racing commitments in Europe's premier sports car series with a Formula One reserve role at Haas, having appeared in seven championship rounds during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. Previously driving for AlphaTauri, he achieved a significant victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar is a Franco-Algerian motorsport competitor who races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, representing France internationally.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver competing for Ferrari who holds an unprecedented seven world championship titles, equaling Michael Schumacher's record. The accomplished competitor also boasts the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg, a German driver, currently races in Formula One for Audi. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved significant success in endurance motorsport, notably securing victory at the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born motorsport competitor who currently races for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Monaco-born Charles Leclerc drives for Ferrari in Formula One, where he finished as championship runner-up in 2022. The driver has accumulated nine Grand Prix victories over his nine seasons in the sport.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen, a Danish driver, competed in Formula One across two separate periods from 2014 to 2020 and again from 2022 to 2024. Currently, he races for BMW in the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT while also pursuing a part-time NASCAR Cup Series career with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently racing for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship with the team. Throughout his eight seasons in the sport, he has secured eleven Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French motorsport competitor currently racing for Haas in Formula One, having previously secured a victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One. A veteran of 15 seasons, Pérez finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while with Red Bull and has secured six race victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having accumulated nine Grand Prix victories since his entry into the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger", competed in Formula One over a 14-year span from 2011 until 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having claimed seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant competed in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 machinery in IMSA competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Canadian driver Lance Stroll currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, bringing his competitive spirit to one of the sport's most prestigious teams.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, has been involved in Formula One racing since 2021, currently holding a reserve driver position with Red Bull Racing and its sister team Racing Bulls.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver has claimed four consecutive world championships from 2021 to 2024 while racing for Red Bull Racing, establishing himself among Formula One's most successful competitors with 71 Grand Prix victories accumulated over his 12-season career.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is the sole Chinese driver to have participated in Formula One, having raced in the series from 2022 through 2024. He currently holds a reserve driver position with Cadillac in the championship.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has raced as Alpine since 2021, inheriting Renault's works entry following a rebranding to promote the French carmaker's sports car division. Alpine's sole Formula One victory came through Esteban Ocon at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, with the team operating Mercedes power units and competing under a French licence until Renault's departure from the sport in 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has competed in Formula One through multiple team entities, with the current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco branding in the sport.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, holds the distinction of being Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team, participating in every World Championship since the sport's inaugural 1950 season. The squad, nicknamed "the Prancing Horse" after their iconic emblem, remains a foundational institution in Formula One racing history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One team founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas, the squad commenced racing in the 2016 season with Ayao Komatsu currently serving as team principal following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024. The organization has established itself as a competitive midfield presence in the sport since its inception.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Sauber Motorsport AG operated as a Swiss racing engineering firm and constructor founded by Peter Sauber in 1970, initially competing in endurance racing where it secured two world championships and victory at the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours alongside Mercedes-Benz. The outfit competed in Formula One from 1993 until 2025 as an independent team, becoming the fourth-longest-serving constructor by race entries before its assets were purchased by Audi AG in 2024 to form the foundation of Audi's works F1 programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under McLaren Mastercard F1 Team. The team operates as part of the wider McLaren Group, which is owned by Bahrain's Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier. The current Mercedes-AMG Petronas team, based in Brackley under a German licence, has been jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Toto Wolff, and Ineos since 2022, with the squad historically known as the "Silver Arrows.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that commenced competition in 2024, operating as one of two Red Bull-owned entries alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with operations in Milton Keynes, the team represents the Austrian conglomerate's second manufacturer presence on the grid.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024 as the second team operated by Red Bull, alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility in Milton Keynes, the team represents Red Bull's dual-team structure in the championship.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, an Austrian-licensed team headquartered in England, is one of two Formula One operations controlled by Red Bull GmbH. Founded in 2005 and long managed by Christian Horner, the team transitioned to Laurent Mekies' leadership in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Atlassian Williams F1 Team is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's previous failed racing venture. The team operates from a substantial facility in Grove, Oxfordshire, and has competed continuously in the sport since its inception.
